卡恰皮琴主要出現在西爪哇巽他音樂場合：作為巽他歌曲（tembang Sunda）: The kacapi appears mainly in Sundanese music of West Java: it is the main accompanying instrument for Sundanese song (tembang Sunda) and for the Mamaos Cianjuran repertoire; in the kacapi-and-flute ensemble (kacapi suling, in Indonesian kecapi seruling) it plays with the flute and no voice; it is also used for pantun story chanting, and as an additional instrument in gamelan degung performances. The Baduy Sundanese of Banten province still accompany pantun stories with the kacapi alone. By accompanying role it divides into the kacapi indung, which leads, and the kacapi rincik, which fills in the high register.
卡恰皮琴主要採用優質木材製作琴身共鳴箱，通常選用聲學特性優良的當地硬木。琴弦由絲: The kacapi's soundbox is made of good-quality wood, usually a local hardwood with good acoustic properties. The strings are silk or nylon and resonate well. The soundboard is thin, springy wood, which strengthens the resonance of the timbre. The posts are hardwood, to take the string tension. Some kacapi are decorated with woodcarving or traditional patterns at the neck. The whole structure is carefully finished so that the tone stays pure and warm.
卡恰皮琴是印尼巽他地區的傳統古箏，起源於爪哇西部的巽他族文化。這件樂器與中國古箏: The kacapi is a traditional zither of the Sundanese region of Indonesia, rooted in the Sundanese culture of western Java. The instrument shares structural features with East Asian instruments such as the Chinese guzheng, the Japanese koto, the Mongolian yangqin and the Korean gayageum, a sign of the deep influence of ancient Silk Road trade on regional instruments. In the course of Sundanese culture the kacapi gradually became an important traditional instrument and a central part of the local musical tradition.
卡恰皮琴是印尼西爪哇巽他人的傳統齊特琴，霍恩博斯特尔—薩克斯編號314.122，: The kacapi is the traditional zither of the Sundanese of West Java, Indonesia, Hornbostel–Sachs 314.122, a chordophone. The body comes in a boat-shaped and a flat soundbox form, with holes in the base, and the strings are fixed to pegs at the upper right; modern soundboxes are mostly glued from boards. Players traditionally sit on the floor with the strings about twenty-five centimetres above it, and the instrument can also rest on a wooden stand. It is used for Sundanese song, Mamaos Cianjuran, kacapi suling, pantun story chanting, and as an additional instrument in gamelan degung.
卡恰皮琴音色溫潤而富有詩意，具有明亮而不刺耳的特質。其音域寬廣，能夠演奏高低起伏: The kacapi's timbre is warm and poetic, bright without being harsh. Its range is wide and it can play melodies that rise and fall; the top register sounds clear and transparent, while the middle and low registers have a warm, solid texture. The resonance of the vibrating strings is deep and lasting, and in the soundbox the timbre gains layers, with a soft sense of extension. Beside the Chinese guzheng the kacapi sounds a little more reserved and inward; beside the Japanese koto its sound has the warmer feel of Southeast Asia. In an ensemble it can lead with a clear, firm melody or blend into the background as an accompanying instrument, producing an elegant sound with carrying power.
隨著時間推移，卡恰皮琴的應用範圍不斷擴展。它在巽他歌唱表演中充當主要伴奏樂器，也: Over time the uses of the kacapi have kept widening. It serves as the main accompanying instrument in Sundanese song performance, and is also used for Mamaos verse recitation, for kecapi seruling (the type with no vocal accompaniment) and for pantun story recitation. In the gamelan degung ensemble it takes the role of an auxiliary instrument. Through these varied uses the kacapi holds an important place in Sundanese musical practice and cultural transmission, and it remains an important emblem of Indonesian traditional music.
